stem: What does infrastructure as code mean?

choices.A: Replace Azure role assignments with comments
choices.B: Describe and manage infrastructure using versioned code or templates
choices.C: Create resources only through undocumented clicks
choices.D: Store application passwords in source files

explanations.A: Comments do not authorize operations.
explanations.B: Infrastructure definitions become reviewable artifacts.
explanations.C: That does not preserve an executable definition.
explanations.D: Secrets are not the purpose of infrastructure as code.

stem: A team wants to reproduce a test network with the same configuration next week. Which practice helps?

choices.A: Use a manual checklist without capturing parameter values
choices.B: Keep its declarative definition in version control
choices.C: Use only a cost forecast for the project
choices.D: Record only the resource group's display name

explanations.A: Incomplete inputs make repeated results harder to reproduce.
explanations.B: A reviewed definition records the intended configuration.
explanations.C: Financial estimates do not specify the deployed network.
explanations.D: A name omits the network's required configuration.

stem: What does a declarative template emphasize?

choices.A: Every manual mouse movement
choices.B: The desired resource state
choices.C: Only the resource's monthly invoice
choices.D: The user's authentication-factor history

explanations.A: That is not declarative infrastructure.
explanations.B: The platform interprets the definition to deploy that state.
explanations.C: Invoices record charges rather than desired configuration.
explanations.D: That is identity evidence.

stem: Why parameterize a template's location?

choices.A: The same definition can be reused with an explicit region value
choices.B: The deployment becomes independent of service availability
choices.C: Every parameter value is a secret
choices.D: The parameter grants subscription Owner

explanations.A: Parameters separate environment inputs from reusable resource logic.
explanations.B: The chosen region still must support the resource.
explanations.C: A region identifier is normally non-sensitive configuration.
explanations.D: Parameters do not grant permissions.

stem: Which benefit does code review provide for an infrastructure change?

choices.A: A replacement for postdeployment validation
choices.B: Automatic removal of every resource lock
choices.C: A guarantee that no runtime operation can fail
choices.D: A chance to inspect intended configuration before deployment

explanations.A: Actual state still needs verification.
explanations.B: Review does not change Azure.
explanations.C: Permissions, policies, and services can still cause failures.
explanations.D: Review can identify unexpected resource or security changes.

stem: What is configuration drift?

choices.A: A user forgets an MFA method
choices.B: The VM moves physically while running
choices.C: The billing currency changes on every API call
choices.D: Actual resource settings diverge from the intended definition

explanations.A: That is an identity-management issue.
explanations.B: That is not the meaning of configuration drift.
explanations.C: That is not expected drift behavior.
explanations.D: Manual or external changes can create drift.

stem: An operator manually changes a network prefix after a template deployment. What should the team do?

choices.A: Delete all unrelated resource groups
choices.B: Assume the template file was automatically updated
choices.C: Compare the actual state with the reviewed definition
choices.D: Ignore the difference because the name is unchanged

explanations.A: That is unrelated and destructive.
explanations.B: Azure does not rewrite local source to match every manual change.
explanations.C: The difference may need reconciliation or an intentional code change.
explanations.D: Names alone do not prove configuration consistency.

stem: Which item should remain outside a public infrastructure repository?

choices.A: Credentials and access tokens
choices.B: A subnet address prefix used for a training scenario
choices.C: A non-sensitive region parameter name
choices.D: A description of the intended resource types

explanations.A: Secrets must not be published.
explanations.B: An invented lab address range is not inherently a credential.
explanations.C: That can be part of reviewed source.
explanations.D: That is useful documentation.

stem: Why include a validation step after deployment?

choices.A: Validation moves resources to a cheaper region
choices.B: Validation grants missing RBAC permissions
choices.C: Successful submission does not prove every learning requirement is met
choices.D: Validation eliminates all usage charges

explanations.A: That is not a read-only validation action.
explanations.B: It should observe rather than grant access.
explanations.C: Validation inspects the resulting state.
explanations.D: Reading state does not stop meters.

stem: What does a deployment preview help with?

choices.A: Guaranteeing a deployment will succeed later
choices.B: Creating the network without an execute action
choices.C: Making chargeable resources free
choices.D: Understanding expected changes before execution

explanations.A: Environment and permissions can still change.
explanations.B: A preview should not perform the change.
explanations.C: Preview does not alter service pricing.
explanations.D: Preview improves reviewability.

stem: A resource name and scope remain the same on redeployment. What is a common declarative outcome?

choices.A: The subscription is canceled
choices.B: The existing resource is evaluated and updated toward the definition
choices.C: All resources outside the template are always deleted
choices.D: A duplicate is always created with a random name

explanations.A: Redeployment does not cancel subscriptions.
explanations.B: The resource identity is not recreated under a new name automatically.
explanations.C: Deletion behavior depends on deployment mechanisms and modes.
explanations.D: Stable identities avoid that automatic duplication.

stem: Which artifact best supports a repeatable network change request?

choices.A: Only a subscription budget
choices.B: Only a deployment-record name
choices.C: A version-controlled template diff with explicit parameter values
choices.D: A portal screenshot that omits prefixes and deployment inputs

explanations.A: A spending threshold does not define infrastructure state.
explanations.B: The record label does not describe the proposed configuration.
explanations.C: This records both the intended change and its environment inputs.
explanations.D: That cannot specify the complete intended network change.

stem: Why should deployment inputs be explicit in a learning script?

choices.A: They make a template exempt from Azure Policy
choices.B: They make the target subscription, region, and run unambiguous
choices.C: They automatically approve every future deployment
choices.D: They remove provider registration requirements

explanations.A: Policies still evaluate requests.
explanations.B: Explicit inputs reduce accidental use of defaults.
explanations.C: Inputs are not blanket authorization.
explanations.D: Resources still require supported providers.

stem: How should a team handle an intentional infrastructure change found during drift review?

choices.A: Remove all validation because state changed
choices.B: Publish the operator's token as evidence
choices.C: Silently overwrite source with every observed setting
choices.D: Update and review the definition before applying the agreed state

explanations.A: Changed state makes validation more useful.
explanations.B: Tokens should remain private.
explanations.C: Not every change is intended or safe.
explanations.D: Source should reflect the intended architecture.

stem: What does offline validation of this IaC lab establish?

choices.A: The source and safeguards were checked without a live Azure deployment
choices.B: No deployment can ever incur a charge
choices.C: Every Azure region has been deployed successfully
choices.D: The learner's RBAC roles are sufficient

explanations.A: It supports readiness while leaving live behavior to learner testing.
explanations.B: Actual resources and usage determine costs.
explanations.C: Offline checks cannot prove that.
explanations.D: Live authorization has not been verified.

stem: What is Azure Resource Manager's role?

choices.A: A protocol for employee passwordless sign-in
choices.B: The management layer for deploying and organizing Azure resources
choices.C: The guest operating system inside every VM
choices.D: A replacement for all application data APIs

explanations.A: That is an identity concern.
explanations.B: ARM handles resource management requests.
explanations.C: ARM is not a guest OS.
explanations.D: Data-plane services have their own interfaces.

stem: Which tools can send resource-management requests to ARM?

choices.A: Only Entra guest invitations
choices.B: The Azure portal, CLI, PowerShell, and APIs
choices.C: Only the Azure portal
choices.D: Only Storage Explorer file uploads

explanations.A: Identity invitations are not the complete resource-management scope.
explanations.B: These interfaces can use the resource management layer.
explanations.C: ARM is accessible through several tools.
explanations.D: Data uploads are not its only or defining interface.

stem: What is an ARM template?

choices.A: An MFA authentication method
choices.B: A declarative JSON description for Azure deployments
choices.C: A CSV of Azure invoices
choices.D: A compressed copy of every VM disk

explanations.A: Templates do not verify users.
explanations.B: The template describes intended resources and related deployment inputs.
explanations.C: That is billing data.
explanations.D: That is a backup artifact.

stem: How does Bicep relate to ARM templates?

choices.A: Bicep is an identity directory
choices.B: Bicep is a declarative language compiled for ARM deployment
choices.C: Bicep bypasses Azure policies and permissions
choices.D: Bicep is a separate cloud provider

explanations.A: It does not manage directory sign-in.
explanations.B: It offers concise authoring over the same deployment platform.
explanations.C: Deployment checks still apply.
explanations.D: It targets Azure infrastructure.

stem: A Bicep file declares targetScope='resourceGroup'. Where is that template intended to deploy?

choices.A: At subscription scope
choices.B: At management-group scope
choices.C: At resource-group scope
choices.D: At tenant scope

explanations.A: Subscription scope would require a subscription-targeted deployment definition.
explanations.B: Management-group scope is a different explicit Bicep deployment target.
explanations.C: The target scope specifies the deployment boundary.
explanations.D: Tenant scope is distinct from the declared resource-group target.

stem: What does a resource's API version specify in Bicep?

choices.A: The resource-provider contract used for its properties
choices.B: The version of the workload's guest operating system
choices.C: The Bicep CLI's installed version
choices.D: The deployment mode incremental or complete

explanations.A: API versions define supported schema and behavior.
explanations.B: The OS version is not the Azure resource schema version.
explanations.C: The compiler version is different from the resource provider's API contract.
explanations.D: Deployment mode controls deployment behavior rather than the resource API contract.

stem: What does a template output provide?

choices.A: Automatic Contributor access for every reader
choices.B: A guarantee of zero monthly cost
choices.C: A replacement for the resource ID hierarchy
choices.D: A deployment result such as a created resource's name

explanations.A: Outputs do not grant access.
explanations.B: Outputs are not pricing controls.
explanations.C: They can report identifiers without replacing the hierarchy.
explanations.D: Outputs expose useful values after evaluation.

stem: What can ARM use to order related resource deployment?

choices.A: The resource display names alone
choices.B: Resource dependencies
choices.C: The expected monthly cost of each resource
choices.D: The order in which operators last viewed resources in the portal

explanations.A: Names identify resources but do not fully express deployment dependency relationships.
explanations.B: Dependencies help ensure prerequisites are deployed before dependent resources.
explanations.C: Price is not ARM's dependency ordering mechanism.
explanations.D: Observation order does not define the template's resource dependencies.

stem: What does az bicep build perform?

choices.A: Compile the Bicep source to an ARM template locally
choices.B: Start an application telemetry workspace
choices.C: Create the VNet in Azure
choices.D: Assign Reader to the learner

explanations.A: Compilation checks authoring without deploying resources.
explanations.B: That is unrelated to compilation.
explanations.C: Build is not a deployment command.
explanations.D: Compilation does not change roles.

stem: What does a group deployment require in addition to a valid template?

choices.A: A public storage access key in Git
choices.B: A guarantee that the user is Entra Global Administrator
choices.C: Every resource must already exist in another cloud
choices.D: A target resource group and appropriate deployment permissions

explanations.A: Public secrets are unnecessary.
explanations.B: That role is not a universal resource deployment prerequisite.
explanations.C: That is not an ARM requirement.
explanations.D: Syntax validity alone does not provide scope or authorization.

stem: What does ARM what-if aim to show?

choices.A: A guaranteed future invoice
choices.B: Every possible guest sign-in
choices.C: All application requests after deployment
choices.D: Predicted resource changes for a proposed deployment

explanations.A: It previews configuration changes rather than exact bills.
explanations.B: It is not an identity simulator.
explanations.C: That is telemetry rather than deployment preview.
explanations.D: It helps inspect a deployment's expected effects.

stem: The lab template declares vnet-az900 and subnet-default. Which validation matches it?

choices.A: Verify that a VM was created automatically
choices.B: Inspect the VNet and subnet names and address prefixes
choices.C: Verify that every tenant guest became an Owner
choices.D: Verify that a paid Purview scan was enabled

explanations.A: The template does not declare a VM.
explanations.B: These properties demonstrate the deployed network matches the definition.
explanations.C: The template does not assign those roles.
explanations.D: The template does not declare that service.

stem: Why can a valid Bicep template still fail during Azure deployment?

choices.A: Permissions, policy, provider support, or quota may block it
choices.B: Valid source automatically bypasses resource locks
choices.C: Compilation guarantees all live prerequisites
choices.D: ARM ignores the selected subscription

explanations.A: Local syntax success is only one requirement.
explanations.B: Applicable locks still matter.
explanations.C: It does not verify every environment condition.
explanations.D: Deployment remains scoped.

stem: An incremental deployment omits an unrelated resource already in the group. What should a beginner generally expect?

choices.A: Every omitted resource is always deleted
choices.B: The omitted resource becomes a tenant user
choices.C: The resource moves to a new subscription
choices.D: Omission alone does not delete that unrelated resource

explanations.A: That describes neither general incremental behavior nor the safe lab intent.
explanations.B: Deployment omission does not change resource types.
explanations.C: Omission does not imply a move.
explanations.D: Incremental mode does not remove resources simply because they are absent.

stem: Which distinction separates a resource group from an ARM deployment record?

choices.A: A group is only a JSON compiler output
choices.B: The deployment record is the customer's identity directory
choices.C: Deleting a deployment record necessarily deletes every deployed resource
choices.D: The group contains resources; the deployment record reports a deployment operation

explanations.A: Groups are Azure management containers.
explanations.B: That is the tenant.
explanations.C: The record and resource lifetimes differ.
explanations.D: A deployment is not a replacement for its resource container.
